- Cation: Na+

   - OH- would make the solution basic (pH > 7) - eliminate
   - CO3-2 would make the solution basic (pH > 7) - eliminate
   - S-2 would make the solution basic (pH > 7) - eliminate
   - HS- would make the solution basic (pH > 7) - eliminate
   - PO4-3 would make the solution basic (pH > 7) - eliminate
   - HPO4-2 would make the solution slightly basic (pH > 7) - eliminate
   - HSO4- would make the solution acidic (pH < 7) - eliminate
   - HCrO4- would make the solution acidic (pH < 7) - eliminate (also already eliminated by color)
   
   Neutral salts of Na+ (pH ≈ 7):
   - NaCl, NaBr, NaI, NaNO3, Na2SO4, NaF, NaHCO3, NaH2PO4

3. **Combining both criteria:**
   - Anions that form colorless, neutral solutions with Na+:
   - Cl-, Br-, I-, NO3-, SO4-2, F-, HCO3-, H2PO4-

Let me verify this list makes sense:
- Halides (Cl-, Br-, I-, F-): neutral salts with Na+, colorless ✓
- NO3-: neutral salt with Na+, colorless ✓
- SO4-2: neutral salt with Na+, colorless ✓
- HCO3-: slightly basic but can be close to neutral ✓
- H2PO4-: slightly acidic but can be close to neutral ✓

The narrowed down list should be: Br-, Cl-, F-, HCO3-, H2PO4-, I-, NO3-, SO4-2
</thought>
